title: Session Multiplexing PRD Sketch
summary: Brainstorm / rough PRD for a feature that safely multiplexes multiple logical sessions onto fewer runtime contexts to reduce cost and improve throughput without breaking session isolation guarantees.
content:
Problem statement:
Many customers keep lots of warm sessions (chat histories, embeddings caches, user KV caches) pinned to dedicated runtime contexts which increases GPU memory pressure and idle token compute. For low-traffic users this results in wasted capacity and higher unit cost.

Hypothesis / goal:
If we can multiplex low-rate logical sessions onto shared runtime shards without exposing cross-session state, we can reduce required memory footprint and improve GPU utilization, cutting per-session cost by 20-40% for tail workloads while keeping P95 latency and quality within SLOs.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT session merging: we must preserve logical isolation (no cross-user leakage).
- Not targeting heavy real-time streams where per-session latency is critical (initial focus: background assistants, low-freq chat).

Constraints and guardrails:
- Must maintain customer-configured data isolation; private deployments may opt-out or require explicit policy.
- Audit logs must still be emitted with session identifiers.
- KV cache and prefix state are namespaced; no sharing of raw KV pointers across sessions.
- Fallback to dedicated context on mismatch or QoS breach.

Core idea / approach:
1) Logical session descriptor: lightweight metadata (session-id, customer-id, model, max-context, affinity tags).
2) Multiplexing pool: a pool of runtime contexts that accept multiple logical sessions. Each runtime keeps per-session isolated KV and prefix regions in memory via memory-segmentation and virtualized pointer tables.
3) Time-slicing / batching policy: scheduled micro-batches per runtime where requests from multiple sessions are batched when compatible (same model variant & quantization).
4) Eviction and pinning: sessions can be pinned to dedicated contexts (e.g., VIP customers, active sessions). Idle sessions are candidates for multiplexing.
5) Safety envelope: per-session resource caps and anomaly detectors (token spikes, hallucination rate, latency regression). If thresholds exceeded, move session to dedicated runtime and trigger alert.

User stories:
- As an infra engineer, I want idle customer sessions to be automatically placed into multiplex pools so we reduce reserved contexts and lower cost.
- As a product owner, I want canaries to validate that multiplexing does not alter output distributions for our core prompts.
- As an enterprise admin, I want the option to opt-out specific workspaces from multiplexing.
- As an SRE, I need telemetry that shows multiplexing ratio, per-session latency delta, and eviction rates.

Success metrics (initial):
- Cost: reduce idle-context GPU memory footprint by 25% for customers with <1 req/min session traffic.
- Quality: change in prompt-level generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim) < 1% for monitored evaluation sets.
- Latency: P95 end-to-end latency delta <= 10% for multiplexed sessions vs baseline.
- Stability: < 0.5% of sessions require emergency fallback per week.

Telemetry / dashboards needed:
- Multiplexing coverage (% sessions multiplexed by tier/region)
- Average sessions per runtime, distribution tail (99th percentile)
- Eviction reasons and time-to-recover
- Per-customer cost delta and token accounting
- Regression alerts linked to eval prompt sets

Experiment plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
Alpha (internal): small pool in us-west, only for low-rate test tenants. Manual rollout, heavy logging, no SLA.
Beta (selected customers): opt-in button in Console, expose telemetry, run A/B on quality.
GA: enabled by default for eligible non-enterprise tenants; UI controls for opt-outs and pinning.

Implementation notes / perf considerations:
- Memory model: use per-session compacted KV representation; coalesce similar prefix encodings to reduce duplication but maintain per-session view via copy-on-write.
- Batching: request routing should prefer merging requests with same model/config; avoid batching when request latency budget is very tight.
- Kernel warmups: multiplexing may increase model-context churn; prefetching strategies for likely re-activation sessions could help.

Security / compliance:
- All data remains in customer namespace; no hardware-level co-tenancy change for private deployments.
- For regulated customers, require explicit consent or dedicated-only policy.

Open questions / risks:
- How to quantify subtle quality regressions introduced by micro-batching across sessions? Need eval harness that mirrors customer prompt diversity.
- Memory accounting complexity for large KV caches with many small sessions.
- Edge case: multi-turn sessions with long-tail spikes (user returns after hours with huge context) — eviction vs prefetch trade-offs.
- Billing model: how to reflect multiplexing in per-token or per-session pricing fairly?

Next steps / short-term action items:
- Spike: prototype in serving-runtime repo to simulate 1000 low-rate sessions multiplexed onto 10 contexts; measure latency, GPU mem, and KV overhead (owner: Marco).
- Telemetry: define minimal logs and Prometheus metrics (owner: Nina).
- Console: stub opt-in UI & admin opt-out flag (frontend sketch).
- Eval: assemble 50 customer-like prompt sets to be used for canary quality checks.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Might combine with existing "idle-session-eviction" heuristics; re-using cache keys could be a win.
- Consider a lightweight session fingerprint to group highly-similar sessions onto same runtime to improve cache hits.
notes: This is rough; intended as a personal working doc for early alignment. Will convert to a more formal PRD if spike results look promising.
